insider_note: The x = tanθ substitution is the key step: once it is made, this integral becomes ∫ log(1 + tanθ) dθ from 0 to π/4. Recognising that form saves re-deriving the tan(A−B) algebra from scratch.

steps.label: Substitute x = tanθ
steps.margin_note: First two marks. 1 + x² becomes sec²θ, which cancels the sec²θ dθ from dx exactly.
steps.memory_tip: x = tanθ is the standard substitution whenever 1 + x² sits in a denominator.
lines: The 1 + x² underneath suggests x = tanθ,
Put x = tanθ ⇒ dx = sec²θ dθ
Change the limits with the substitution:
The sec²θ above and below cancel:
steps.why: x = tanθ turns 1 + x² into sec²θ, which exactly cancels the sec²θ that comes from dx — the whole denominator vanishes, leaving a plain log(1+tanθ) integral in the new variable θ.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to change the limits from x = 0, 1 to θ = 0, π/4.
Not cancelling the sec²θ from the numerator (dx) with the sec²θ in the denominator (1+x²).

steps.label: Apply the property and simplify tan(π/4 − θ)
steps.margin_note: Three marks. The θ → π/4 − θ property and the tan(A−B) identity do all the work here.
steps.memory_tip: tan(π/4 − θ) = (1 − tanθ)/(1 + tanθ). Adding 1 to it gives 2/(1 + tanθ).
steps.why: Once the integral is written in θ it is ∫ log(1 + tanθ) dθ from 0 to π/4, and the θ → π/4 − θ property with the tan(A−B) identity reduces it to (π/4)log2 − I.
common_mistakes: Re-deriving the algebra with the wrong variable name and losing track of which step is which.
Skipping the log-splitting step log[2/(1+tanθ)] = log2 − log(1+tanθ).

steps.label: Solve for I
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. I appears on both sides, so collect it and divide by 2.
steps.memory_tip: Add I to both sides of I = (π/4)log2 − I to get 2I = (π/4)log2.

lines.text: Take the I on the right to the left side:

steps.why: Adding I to both sides gives 2I directly, and dividing by 2 gives (π/8)log2 — the same value as ∫ log(1 + tanθ) dθ from 0 to π/4, which is what step 1 showed this integral equals.
common_mistakes: Reporting a value other than (π/8)log2 without checking the arithmetic of 2I = (π/4)log2.
